layers.name: Console
layers.head: Tracks that know about each other
layers.body: Set each strip to Stem, Bus or Master and it links up with the strips on your other tracks. The Rail Link meter lights up when the link is live.. I still get a kick out of watching that. Pick a console flavour (Signature, Vintage British, Discrete American, Modern Ultra-Linear or Custom), and every Stem gets its own Mixer, so you can tweak one track from another.

layers.name: Rail
layers.head: Shared flow between instances
layers.body: Rail coupling passes level and energy between linked strips, so the whole mix moves together like it's running through one console. The display has 11 analyzer styles, from Ribbon and Waterfall to SPIRALS: a spectrum fountain with a resonance finder that points at the trouble spots.

layers.name: Neural
layers.head: Bring your own captures
layers.body: Swap the Console's built-in saturation for a neural capture. Load .nam or .json files through the tone browser, or import files and packs. Drive sets how hard you hit the capture, Mix blends it against the Console's own saturation. Heads up: I don't include any captures, so bring your favourites.

layers.name: Dynamics
layers.head: Voicings, or build your own
layers.body: Pick a compressor voicing, or switch to CUSTOM and put one together from 35 parts in seven slots. A lot of those parts I fitted to analysis of real units. The voicings are VCA, FET, Opto, Tube and Diode, and most have sub-modes of their own. There's also a Gate/Expand and De-Ess section with five voicings (wideband or split-band de-essing), an external sidechain, and everything runs stereo or mid-side.
layers.spec: 5 voicings · CUSTOM parts · gate · de-ess · M/S

layers.name: EQ
layers.head: Classic curves, band by band
layers.body: The bells and shelves follow curves fitted to analysis of classic EQs. In CUSTOM, each of the four bands takes its own part, so you can mix and match per band. On top of that: six EQ voicings, series or parallel, stereo or mid-side. And the new Macro curve sits before the bands.. one pivot, Tilt and Smile, with its own slope and spread, four parts (Clean, Iron, Shelf Pair and Passive Lift), an optional dynamic mode, and a handle right on the graph.

layers.name: Finisher
layers.head: Colour, tape and clipping
layers.body: Lysium is preamp-style colour: even or odd harmonics, low-end weight, and treble that softens as you push it. Logos is a tube-style saturator, A-Roll is tape (15 or 30 IPS, with a heat control), Tarus is a clipper, and Kill is a clipper at the very end. Nerd note: Lysium, Logos, Tarus and Kill oversample up to 16x.. tape doesn't.

layers.name: Limiter
layers.head: True-peak limiting
layers.body: Three modes for three jobs. I drove it 18 dB past full scale and the output still stopped at the −1 dBTP ceiling.

layers.name: Filter types
layers.head: Twelve filters I designed myself
layers.body: Drive, Bite, Comb +, Comb −, Formant, Twin, Wave, Fold, Square, Crush, Ladder and Cascade. A Movement section (envelope, LFO and follower) sweeps the cutoff around.

layers.name: Modes
layers.head: Eight modes
layers.body: Drive, Bite, Twin and Wave give you LP 24, LP 12, BP 12, HP 12, HP 24, BP 24, Notch and All-pass. Nerd note: Bite builds its 24 dB modes from two stacked state-variable stages, with a clipped resonance.

layers.name: Resonance
layers.head: A peak that sings
layers.body: Resonance raises a peak at the cutoff, and on the Drive filter the bass thins out as it climbs. The plots further down show the curves if you want to see it.

layers.name: Comb ±
layers.head: Two combs in one
layers.body: Crossfade from a feedforward comb into a feedback comb. I put a soft ceiling in the feedback loop so it stays under control.. mostly.

layers.name: Stage order
layers.head: Six orders
layers.body: Filter, Chorus and Delay run in one of six orders, picked from a list. Chorus has four styles, and the delay works in note lengths, with feedback, tone and ping-pong.

layers.name: Drive
layers.head: Drive and a soft ceiling
layers.body: Drive pushes the signal into one of nine saturation curves. The output ends in a soft ceiling, with an optional Auto Gain. Filter oversampling goes Off, 2x, 4x or 8x.

layers.name: Engine A
layers.head: Ten shapes, or eight pedals
layers.body: Pick a shape, set Drive and Bias, and the scope draws the transfer curve live as you turn them. Or switch Engine A to a pedal: Clean Boost, Tight Boost, Overdrive, Fuzz, Filter Distortion, Distortion, Metal or Octave Fuzz, each with Drive, Tone and Level. I fitted those to analysis and community captures of real pedals.

layers.name: Engine B
layers.head: The same ten shapes, picked independently
layers.body: Engine B has the same ten shapes as Engine A, with its own selector and controls. A couple of my favourite details: Diode bends harder on one side than the other, and Rectify slides from half-wave to full-wave as you raise Bias.

layers.name: Routing
layers.head: Five ways to wire them
layers.body: Serial, Parallel, Stereo (A left, B right), Mid/Side (A mid, B side) or Band Split (A low, B high), with a feedback loop wrapped around the pair.

layers.name: Oversampling
layers.head: Clean at the top
layers.body: Quality sets oversampling from 1x to 8x, so hard-driven tones alias less. The exception is Crush.. that one aliases on purpose.

layers.name: Capture
layers.head: A capture after the engines
layers.body: Load a neural capture (.nam) of an amp or pedal after the two engines, with a gate and a tight, mid or bright voicing in front of it.

layers.name: Cab
layers.head: Two cabs, blended
layers.body: Load two cab impulse responses and blend between them, with low and high cuts.
layers.spec: Cab A / B · low cut · high cut

layers.name: Units
layers.head: Six units, fitted to analysis
layers.body: Each unit is my own reverb, fitted to the analyzed decay and colour of a classic digital reverb: Megha, Guha, Vayu, Dvaya, Valuka and Adi. The plots below show their reverb time band by band. And the FIT switch lets you compare the original fit with my newer refit of the late reverb, done from analysis.
layers.spec: Megha · Guha · Vayu · Dvaya · Valuka · Adi

layers.name: Converters
layers.head: Optional vintage converters
layers.body: Set Converters to Vintage and a unit adds the word length, word noise, idle floor and DC of old converters, so quiet tails fade into a floor instead of into nothing. It's on Megha (on by default), Valuka and Adi (off by default).

layers.name: Slots
layers.head: Three slots in a row
layers.body: Early, Mid and Late each hold any unit and feed the next. Every slot has pre-delay, width, low and high cuts, shimmer and freeze. Late is always on; Early and Mid start switched off.

layers.name: Wet bus
layers.head: Shape the wet signal
layers.body: After the slots: a four-band wet EQ, ducking, chorus and a fidelity control, with presets and A/B so you can compare settings.

layers.name: No colour
layers.head: No grain added
layers.body: Shunya's units add no saturation, drive or converter grain of their own. That's what I mean by transparent: the space, with nothing layered on top.

layers.name: Units
layers.head: Six units, fitted to analysis
layers.body: Each unit is my own reverb, fitted to the analyzed behaviour of a classic reverb: Mandapa, Vistara, Taranga, Dhvani, Kosha and Chatur. Some add motion or a chorus, and Dhvani and Kosha can feed theirs into the reverb. And the FIT switch lets you compare the original fit with my newer refit of the late reverb, done from analysis.
layers.spec: Mandapa · Vistara · Taranga · Dhvani · Kosha · Chatur

layers.name: Decay
layers.head: Decay band by band
layers.body: In most units the highs fade faster than the lows, like in a real room. The plots below show reverb time per band for each unit.

layers.name: Slots
layers.head: Three slots in a row
layers.body: Early, Mid and Late each hold any unit and feed the next, so you can chain a room into a hall.

layers.name: Wet EQ
layers.head: Shape the wet signal
layers.body: A four-band wet EQ after the slots, with presets and A/B to compare settings.
